CONGRANT.TITLE: Equipment: MRI: Track 1 Acquisition of Polytec MSA-600 Micro System Analyzer for Biomedical Engineering
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: Requested Instrument: Polytec MSA-600-X/U Micro System Analyzer ($695,790), state-of-the-art instrument crucial for biomedical engineering research and education the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV). The location of the instrument is the BIO-MEMS Laboratory (Director Caruntu). Servingover 34,000 students, UTRGV is a non-PhD-granting, minority-serving institution with a predominantly Hispanic student body (92%). The university aims to become an emerging research institution and establish a strong biomedical engineering community. This advanced equipment is crucial to preparing students in engineering, science, and medicine by providing hands-on research experiences that can lead to graduate studies, academic roles, or leadership positions in industry. UTRGV is experiencing rapid growth, with increasing student enrollment and the hiring of new faculty. A recently formed Biomedical Engineering(BME) Cluster for research and education includes eight faculty members, four of whom were hired within the past two years. Supporting faculty research development depends on access to cutting-edge infrastructure like the requested analyzer. Securing this grant lays a foundation for attracting external funding and fostering multidisciplinary collaborations. The lack of this instrument currently limits research efforts. This proposal is strongly supported by UTRGV administration, aligning with the university’s strategic goal of building a robust biomedical engineering research and education program.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Immersive Surgical Planning: An AI-Integrated Virtual Reality Platform for Vascular Procedures
Acquisition of a GPU-Enhanced Advanced Computing and Simulation Instrumentation for Interdisciplinary AI Research and Education at the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
(The proposal was a preproposal submitted to UTRGV for an internal competition.)
As UTRGV researchers address critical problems across divers fields that demand the analysis and management of complex, data-intensive problems, the university faces an increasing demand for high-performance computing (HPC) resources to effectively train modern AI models and conduct large-scale simulations. While some HPC resources are available both on and campus, limitations such as long job queues, insufficient graphics processing unit (GPU) memory, and slow interconnects often delay study results by days or force researchers to transfer sensitive data to remote supercomputer facilities. Moreover, while modern large language models (LLMs) are in high demand at UTRGV for a range of applications, existing cloud solutions are costly and pose privacy concerns. To address this gap, the proposal seeks funding to acquire a GPU-Enhanced Advanced Computing and Simulation Instrumentation (GACSI) equipped with the latest NVIDIA B200 GPUs. The B200 GPUs will enable UTRGV to deploy, fine-tune, evaluate, and operate LLMs entirely on campus, significantly reducing waiting times, eliminating cloud-based usage fees, and ensuring the privacy and security of sensitive data. Hosting these models locally will support the development of new hands-on course modules, allowing both undergraduate and graduate students to engage directly with state-of-the-art generative AI.
